title: Sage Intacct Pricing in 2026: What It Actually Costs
summary: Sage does not publish Sage Intacct pricing. Real contracts put the median near $57k/year. Core financials, modules, entities, implementation, and total cost, broken down.
body_markdown:
Sage Intacct is a leading cloud financial management platform for growing and mid-market finance teams, and like most enterprise software, Sage does not publish a price for it. Every deal is a custom quote built from core financials, users, add-on modules, and the number of legal entities, plus a one-time implementation. That makes **Sage Intacct pricing** hard to pin down. This guide pulls together what third-party trackers and real deals show, so you can size a budget before you talk to a rep.


A note on sourcing: Sage publishes no Sage Intacct price list, so the figures below come from third-party trackers, partners, and aggregated real-deal data, and should be treated as directional.


## **How much does Sage Intacct cost?**


> Sage Intacct pricing is quote-based and modular. Based on aggregated real contracts tracked by Vendr, the median Sage Intacct deal is roughly $57,000 per year, with most landing between about $9,000 and $188,000 depending on users, modules, and legal entities. Entry-level core financials start near $9,000 to $15,000 a year, add-on modules commonly run $3,000 to $10,000 each per year, and implementation typically runs one to one-and-three-quarter times the annual subscription.

## **How Sage Intacct pricing works**


Sage Intacct is sold as an annual SaaS subscription, quoted per deployment. The number is assembled from:


- **Core financials.** The base subscription, starting around $9,000 to $15,000 a year for a single user.
- **Users, by type.** Pricing varies by user role, full business users cost more than employee or view-only users, with negotiated full-user rates commonly around $75 to $150 per user per month.
- **Add-on modules.** Advanced Financials, Fixed Assets, Revenue Recognition, Multi-entity and Consolidation, Project Accounting, and Spend Management each add cost, commonly $3,000 to $10,000 a year each.
- **Legal entities.** The first entity is typically included; each additional entity for multi-entity consolidation adds a fee.
- **Implementation.** A separate one-time cost, often one to one-and-three-quarter times the annual subscription.


Because the price scales with modules and entities more than raw seats, the core financials figure understates the real number for a multi-entity finance team.


## **Sage Intacct subscription estimates**


The most credible figure comes from aggregated real contracts.[Vendr](https://www.vendr.com/marketplace/sage-intacct) reports a median annual deal near $56,900 across nearly 200 transactions, ranging from about $9,400 to $188,000. Partners and trackers like[RKL eSolutions](https://www.rklesolutions.com/sage-intacct-cost) and[ERP Research](https://www.erpresearch.com/pricing/sage-intacct) corroborate entry core financials near $9,000 to $15,000 a year and module pricing of $3,000 to $10,000 each.

Those are estimates; your quote depends on users, modules, and entity count. Multi-year deals are commonly reported to carry meaningful discounts.


## **Implementation and total cost of ownership**


Implementation is a separate and significant line. A common partner rule of thumb is that implementation costs one to one-and-three-quarter times the annual subscription, so a $20,000 subscription can mean $20,000 to $35,000 to implement. Simple deployments can run $5,000 to $15,000, typical ones $25,000 to $75,000, and complex multi-entity projects $100,000 and beyond. Add modules, users, and entities to the core, and realistic all-in first-year totals land near $35,000 to $40,000 for a small finance team and $75,000 to $110,000 for a mid-market, multi-entity deployment. For how it fits the wider stack, see[financial systems](https://www.concourse.ai/insights/financial-systems) .


## **What drives Sage Intacct cost up**


- **Modules.** Each add-on, revenue recognition, fixed assets, or project accounting, raises the subscription by several thousand a year.
- **Legal entities.** Multi-entity consolidation beyond the first entity adds a recurring fee.
- **Users.** Full business users cost more than employee or view-only roles.
- **Implementation.** Scope and integrations drive the one-time cost, often more than the first-year subscription.
- **Renewals.** Uplifts of roughly 3% to 8% a year are commonly reported without negotiated price protection.


## **Is Sage Intacct worth the price?**


For a growing or multi-entity finance team that has outgrown QuickBooks, Sage Intacct often is worth it. It is a strong, dimension-based cloud financial platform with real multi-entity consolidation and revenue recognition, and at that stage the capability justifies the cost.


The friction is the same as with any modular ERP: the bill grows as you add modules and entities, and much of what finance wants is the work done, closing, reconciling, and reporting, rather than another module to configure.

## **Frequently asked questions**


### **Does Sage Intacct publish its pricing?**


No. Sage does not publish a Sage Intacct price list. All pricing is quote-based, built from core financials, users, modules, and entities. The figures here come from third-party trackers such as Vendr and partners like RKL eSolutions, not from Sage.


### **How much does Sage Intacct cost per year?**


Based on aggregated real contracts tracked by Vendr, the median Sage Intacct deal is roughly $56,900 per year, with most between about $9,400 and $188,000. Entry core financials start near $9,000 to $15,000 a year, with add-on modules commonly $3,000 to $10,000 each.


### **How much does Sage Intacct implementation cost?**


A common partner rule of thumb is one to one-and-three-quarter times the annual subscription. Simple deployments can run $5,000 to $15,000, typical ones $25,000 to $75,000, and complex multi-entity projects $100,000 and beyond.


### **Why does Sage Intacct get expensive?**


Because it is priced by modules and entities as much as users. Each add-on module adds several thousand a year, each additional legal entity adds a fee, and renewals commonly rise 3% to 8% a year without a negotiated cap.


### **Is Sage Intacct or NetSuite cheaper?**


Both are quote-based. Sage Intacct often starts lower for a finance-only deployment, while NetSuite is a broader ERP that can cost more as you add users and modules, though the right answer depends on your size and needs. ## **The bottom line**


Sage Intacct pricing is modular and quote-only, with a real-contract median near $57,000 a year that scales with modules and legal entities, plus an implementation that often costs more than the first-year subscription. For a growing, multi-entity finance team, that can be money well spent.
